statement: White Buffalo Calf Woman (Ptesáŋwiŋ) brought the Sacred Pipe (Chanunpa) and the Seven Sacred Rites to the Lakota, per Joseph Epes Brown, The Sacred Pipe: Black Elk's Account of the Seven Rites of the Oglala Sioux (University of Oklahoma Press, 1953). The tradition's own internal dating mechanism — the Battiste Good winter count, a Lakota pictographic year-count record — places this founding narrative at roughly 900 CE ("19 generations ago" in oral retellings). This internal date is not externally corroborated by any independent archaeological or documentary method; the material culture of pipe-ceremonialism generally is far older (millennia) but the Lakota division specifically controlled the Pipestone quarry only from c. 1700 CE, so neither anchor directly dates this specific narrative.

sources.citation: Brown, Joseph Epes. The Sacred Pipe: Black Elk's Account of the Seven Rites of the Oglala Sioux. Norman: University of Oklahoma Press, 1953.
sources.author: Joseph Epes Brown

does_not_demonstrate: That the winter-count "19 generations" dating is independently verified by archaeology or an external chronological method, as opposed to being the tradition's own internal claim
